--help.help: show this help message and exit

-H.help: Adds REQUEST_HEADER to the request;  must be in double quotes and can be used multiple times, e.g. -H "Host: example.com"

-a.help: Print statistics of the performed analysis; if the '-u' parameter is omitted they will be global

-b.help: Print overall findings; if omitted detailed ones will be printed

-c.help: Checks URL response HTTP headers for compliance with OWASP 'Secure Headers Project' best practices

-cicd.help: Print analysis for CI/CD processing; optionally, set the minimum required GRADE (E, D, C, B, A, A+)

-df.help: Do not follow redirects; if omitted the last redirection will be the one analyzed

-e.help: Print only TLS/SSL checks; requires the PATH of testssl (https://testssl.sh/)

-f.help: Print fingerprint statistics; if 'FINGERPRINT_TERM' (E.g., 'Google') is omitted the top 20 results will be printed

-g.help: Print guidelines for enabling security HTTP response headers on popular frameworks, servers and services

-grd.help: Print the checks to grade an analysis, along with advice for improvement

-if.help: Analyzes 'INPUT_FILE': curl's '--dump-header' file or HTTP Archive (HAR) file

-l.help: Defines the language for displaying analysis, errors and messages; if omitted, will be printed in English

-lic.help: Print the license for 'humble', along with permissions, limitations and conditions

-o.help: Export the analysis to the specified format; 'all' will export to all formats

-of.help: Exports analysis to 'OUTPUT_FILE'; if omitted the default filename of the parameter '-o' will be used

-op.help: Exports analysis to 'OUTPUT_PATH'; must be absolute. If omitted the PATH of 'humble.py' will be used

-p.help: Use a proxy for the analysis. E.g., 'http://127.0.0.1:8080'. If no port is specified '8080' will be used

-r.help: Print HTTP response headers and a detailed analysis; '-b' parameter will take priority

-s.help: Skips 'deprecated/insecure' and 'missing' checks for the indicated 'SKIP_HEADERS' (separated by spaces)

-u.help: Scheme, host and port to analyze. E.g., https://google.com or https://google.com:443

-ua.help: User-Agent ID from 'additional/user_agents.txt' file to use. '0' will print all and '1' is the default
